newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile court dismisses charges against police chief.
newsitem.headline: Chile court dismisses charges against police chief.

text.p: Chile's Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a special prosecutor's charges that the national police chief and a top government official had obstructed justice in investigations into crimes by a left-wing guerrilla group in the early 1990s.

By a 5-0 vote, the court unanimously threw out the charges against Investigations Police Chief Nelson Mery and former deputy regional development minister Marcelo Schilling, a court secretary told reporters.

Special prosecutor Raquel Camposano had filed charges against the two and ordered their arrest last month for allegedly dragging their feet in investigations into the murder of a right-wing senator, Jaime Guzman.

Guzman, a confidant of former military ruler General Augusto Pinochet, was gunned down by leftist guerrillas outside Santiago's Catholic University where he was a professor. He was one of the key drafters of Chile's 1980 constitution dictated by the Pinochet regime.

The court's ruling was sure to please members of President Eduardo Frei's government, who have accused right-wing politicians and Guzman's family of trumping up charges against Mery and Schilling to embarrass the government.
Camposano also charged Mery and Schilling with obstructing justice in investigations into the 1991 ransom kidnapping of Christian Edwards, son of the owner of the influential newspaper El Mercurio.

Four members of the Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front, a left-wing guerrilla group, who were convicted of involvement in the crimes, were rescued by comrades from a maximum security prison in a jailbreak last week.
